criteria.rationale: For a brand the defining risk is repeat. The founders bring cohort repeat data unprompted (31 -> 34 -> 38% at 90 days) and set a repeat target. They name their own risks (single co-packer, rising paid-social cost, weaker repeat on Jowar puffs) and offer the cohort sheet and co-packer agreement. Two things hold it back: the deck shows only the best cohort, which may be incomplete, and there is no repeat split by channel. Still an application-only read.

evidence.text: 90-day repeat by cohort: 31% (June), 34% (July), 38% (August), 3,100 customers; deck shows only August.
Founders list single co-packer, rising paid social costs and slower Jowar puffs repeat as key risks.
Offer to share cohort sheet and co-packer agreement; 12-month target 45% repeat, 15% contribution.

criteria.rationale: There was a pre-launch survey of 420 parents, and two channels are hands-on and cheap: nutritionist referrals and gym sampling. The founders also track which SKU repeats worse. A survey is not unscalable fieldwork, though, and the application does not describe what they changed in response.

evidence.text: Survey of 420 urban parents, July 2025.
Nutritionist referrals 20% of new customers (CAC INR 210); gyms and sampling 10% (INR 380).
Slower repeat observed on Jowar puffs.

criteria.rationale: The deciding metric (cohort repeat) is present and improving, and above the anecdotal >30% benchmark. Revenue grew from INR 4.8 L to 16.5 L a month at 48% gross margin. But about 70% of new customers come from paid social and promoted quick commerce. The first order does not pay back CAC, LTV:CAC is about 1.8x, and return rate is not given. C001 does not lower the score because repeat is reported.

evidence.text: Monthly revenue 4.8 -> 7.1 -> 10.2 -> 13.0 -> 16.5 INR L (Jun-Oct); INR 72 L cumulative.
90-day repeat 31/34/38% by cohort vs ~37% peer figure and >30% 'strong' benchmark.
Paid social 45% of new customers (INR 410 CAC), quick commerce 25% (INR 290 after promos).
Gross margin 48%, blended CAC INR 340, contribution 11%, LTV:CAC ~1.8x; first order INR 540.

criteria.rationale: Consumers already pay across three working channels: own site 55%, Amazon 25%, quick commerce 20%. All products depend on one co-packer, and contribution by channel is unknown. Tata (Soulfull) and ITC (Yoga Bar) are consolidating the shelf.

evidence.text: Revenue mix: own site 55%, Amazon 25%, quick commerce 20%.
All products made by one co-packer in Hosur.
Tata Soulfull (millet breakfast), ITC-owned Yoga Bar, Slurrp Farm and a crowded healthy-snack shelf.

criteria.rationale: Contribution is positive (11%), and INR 2.5 Cr could plausibly reach INR 40 L a month. But 40% of the raise goes to inventory and working capital. The scaled peer (Slurrp Farm) still loses ~Rs 33 Cr at ~Rs 100 Cr revenue, so later rounds will be large and this cheque risks dilution.

evidence.text: 12-month targets INR 40 L monthly revenue, 15% contribution; 40% of raise to inventory and working capital.
Contribution after CAC and logistics 11%.
Slurrp Farm FY25 revenue Rs 97.5 Cr with Rs 32.67 Cr net loss.

criteria.rationale: The brand, cohort data and nutritionist network do not depend on one person. But the founders articulate no moat, they rely on a co-packer, and three hero SKUs (87% of orders) sit on a shelf where FMCG majors are buying in.

evidence.text: Three hero SKUs = 87% of orders; seven SKUs from one co-packer.
Nutritionist referral channel (20% of new customers).
Shelf consolidating: Tata Soulfull, ITC Yoga Bar.

criteria.rationale: A packaged food brand, squarely in the consumer-brands focus sector, and labelled as such by the founders.

evidence.text: Sector selected Consumer brands; millet breakfast and snacks brand.

criteria.rationale: First institutional round of INR 2.5 Cr at INR 14 Cr post-money, with angels only. The fund can lead it. Revenue is already about INR 2 Cr annualised, so the round could attract competition, but nothing indicates large VCs are involved.

evidence.text: Raising INR 2.5 Cr at INR 14 Cr post; INR 45 L from three angels.
October revenue INR 16.5 L.

criteria.rationale: On paper, category management plus food science and quick-commerce supply chain fit this business, but those are credentials and are capped. What earns the score is building on this problem: a launched brand with INR 72 L revenue and cohort tracking. Both backgrounds are unverifiable. The food-science wording differs slightly between deck and form, which is minor. Shared history between the founders is unknown.

evidence.text: CEO 6 years category/brand at a packaged-food company; COO 5 years supply chain at quick commerce, runs co-packer; first-time founders, team of 9.
Deck 'trained in food science' vs form 'food science degree'.
LinkedIn links and website are placeholders.
INR 72 L revenue since November 2025 launch.

criteria.rationale: Millet better-for-you breakfast is a consensus, crowded category. Tata and ITC have acquired into it, and Slurrp Farm is at scale. The ambition is urban India only, sized from founders' own estimates.

evidence.text: Tata Soulfull, ITC Yoga Bar, Slurrp Farm, crowded shelf.
INR 2,400 household spend is founders' estimate.

gates.detail: Possible overlap with portfolio consumer-food brands, triggered on the false-alarm-preferred rule. Taakat ('Whole Truth for Masses') is a clean-label, better-for-you packaged-food brand, and MomsMade is a clean-label regional snacks brand. Both sell healthy packaged snacks to Indian households, which is the same job, though positioning and audience may differ (Taakat is mass; GrainKind is urban premium millet breakfast). Kushal should confirm with both founders. Also checked: Masterchow (pre-fund, D2C Asian food: different category), Acai Theory (health QSR, not packaged), DressFolk/Salty/Trisu/Everyday/NewMe/Krvvy/CUNIN/Ionic/&Done (non-food brands), Plazza/Cherry/Vaaree (commerce). No other overlap found.
Food brand; there is no dependence on a withdrawn or pending permission. FSSAI licensing is routine and is listed as a verification gap.
Selected Consumer brands, and it is one.
Pre-seed, INR 2.5 Cr at INR 14 Cr post-money, angels only. Within the lead mandate. There is early revenue, but there is no sign of a Series A or large VCs competing.

case_for: The founders bring the brand's deciding metric unprompted: cohort repeat that improves month over month and is above peer benchmarks (R1, R3).
Real revenue (INR 16.5 L in October, 3.4x since June) at 48% gross margin with positive contribution (R3, R5).
Candid about their risks and willing to share the cohort sheet and co-packer agreement (R1).
Squarely in a focus sector, with a team whose experience matches category and supply chain (S1, S3).
case_against: Growth is mostly bought: about 70% of new customers come from paid social or promoted quick commerce. The first order loses money and LTV:CAC is about 1.8x (R3).
Crowded, consolidating category (Tata Soulfull, ITC Yoga Bar, Slurrp Farm) with no articulated moat; three hero SKUs from one co-packer (R6, S4).
Capital intensity: 40% of the raise goes to inventory, and the scaled peer is still heavily loss-making, so this cheque risks being diluted (R5).
Possible overlap with portfolio brands Taakat and MomsMade needs a conversation first (G1).
call_questions: What is 90-day repeat for paid-social-acquired customers vs nutritionist-referred, and for Jowar puffs vs Ragi choco crunch?
Is the August cohort's 38% a full 90 days for every customer, and why does the deck show only that cohort?
What is contribution after CAC and logistics separately for own site, Amazon and quick commerce?
What capacity headroom does the Hosur co-packer have, and when will a second co-packer be qualified?
Tata and ITC now own millet and better-for-you brands with national distribution. Why won't you be out-shelved within two years? (Pressure test on the weakest point.)
what_would_change_our_view: Repeat that holds above ~40% for paid-acquired cohorts, together with a rising share of customers from cheap earned channels (nutritionists, referrals) and positive contribution on each sales channel.
